fix: When a quality word comes right after 'adaxially' or 'abaxially' ('adaxially lucid', 'abaxially glaucous'), the place word should narrow the bearer to that surface. The second-model rule kept the whole blade as the bearer.
reason: 'Lucid' does mean shiny (glistening is right). But the flora says only the upper (adaxial) surface is shiny, not the whole blade.
The bracts are densely pubescent on the outer (abaxial) side. Bract abaxial epidermis plus pubescent is right. Leaving out the colour 'yellowish' is fine.
Each cyme has 4 or 5 flowers. Flower count 4–5 inside the inflorescence is right.
In Juncus the perianth segments are tepals, and they are lanceolate.
The upper leaves are linear. The 'upper' context (FLOPO:0991376) is attached, and linear blade shape is right.
The base of the calyx is (glandular-)pubescent. 'Calyx has part base, pubescent' says that. Dropping 'glandular' loses detail but adds nothing false.

fix: If the record has a frequency slot, it should keep 'rarely' on the second alternative.
reason: The flora gives obtuse as a rare alternative for the leaf apex, so 'apex obtuse' is said by the flora. 'Rarely' is not kept, but the statement is not false without it.
Juncus perianth segments (tepals) are lanceolate.
The peduncles are about 0.5 mm broad. Peduncle width 0.5 mm is right.
The bracts are pubescent towards their tip. 'Bract has part distal region, pubescent' is right.
The leaves have many leaflets and no petiole. Petiole absent is right.
The seeds are not tailed. Seed caudate, negated, is right.

fix: When 'above'/'beneath' refers to leaflets, the bearer should stay the leaflet, with an upper-side part. Swapping in the whole-leaf upper epidermis loses the leaflet.
reason: The flora says the leaflets are glabrous above. Leaf adaxial epidermis covers the whole leaf, including the rachis, which the flora calls pubescent. So the annotation says more than the flora and partly the opposite.
Male flowers are about 1/3 inch across, about 0.85 cm (0.83 is close enough for 'about'). The 'male' context is attached.
The petals have an obtuse apex. The sepal apex is obtuse too, so the reading is true either way.

fix: A trailing 'in the lower leaves' (followed by 'reducing above') limits the measurement to those leaves. It should fill the position slot.
reason: The flora gives 1–1.5 cm only for the petioles of the lower leaves. Without that limit, the length is false for the upper leaves.
The bracts are longer than the pedicel. Bract increased length relative to the pedicel is right.
The leaf base is attenuate.

target: PO_0009081 (higher order inflorescence axis / inflorescence branch)
fix: When 'branches' follows an inflorescence description, it means the inflorescence branches, not the whole inflorescence.
reason: The flora says the branches of the panicle nod in fruit, not the whole inflorescence. Drooping and the fruit-stage context are right.
The petioles are 1–2 mm in diameter.
The involucre is 15–25 mm long in flower. Length plus the flowering stage is right.
The blade shape runs from very narrowly triangular to ovate. The from/to values (triangular, then ovate FLOPO:0991024) and the 'very narrowly' qualifier match the flora.
Thorns and spines are absent. Thorn absent is right.
The female perianth is 3-lobed, so 3 perianth lobes. The female-flower context is left out, but the count is not false without it in this short flower description.
The sepals are obovate or elliptic. Both alternatives are kept.

target: PO_0000033 (fruit valve), with part midvein, quality prominent
fix: In a fruit description, 'valves ... mid-veined' means a midvein on the fruit valve. The rule should not map 'mid-veined' to leaf midvein regardless of the part it is said of.
reason: The flora is about the valves of the silique, not leaves. Leaf midvein is the wrong part.
The second number range is the width: 3–12(–15) dm = 30–120 cm, extreme 150 cm. The numbers are right.
Shrubs or small trees: shrub habit or tree habit. Dropping 'small' is fine.
The leaf margins are slightly involute. Leaf margin plus involute is right. The moss leaf (phyllid) is covered by PO leaf.
The plant is prostrate, decumbent or erect. The 'drier situations' condition is lost, but this either/or list stays true across both habitats (wetter forms are ascending or prostrate).
